phase: Phase C - Core Execution: STS Abuse Simulation
note: All Account IDs, Access Key IDs, Secret Keys and Session Tokens below are redacted or replaced with example/lab-only values per evidence handling policy.

session_log.action: Enumerate target role and extract its trust policy
session_log.observation: Trust policy scopes the Principal to the account root ARN with no sts:ExternalId, aws:SourceIp, or MFA condition. Any authenticated IAM principal within the same account can assume this role.

session_log.action: Inspect trust policy of second-hop role using hop-1 temporary credentials
session_log.observation: Second role trusts the first role's ARN directly, again with no ExternalId or session-duration restriction, enabling role chaining.

session_log.action: Chain to second role (privilege-escalation hop 2) using hop-1 credentials
session_log.command: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=ASIAEXAMPLEHOP1XXXX AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=[REDACTED] AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=[REDACTED] aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/cg-lab-role-console_last_pass_role --role-session-name hop2-session
session_log.observation: Second hop succeeded without additional verification, completing a two-hop chain from a low-privilege lab user to a role with broad administrative permissions.

session_log.action: Verify permissions reachable at end of chain
session_log.observation: Confirms full administrative privilege was reachable in exactly two AssumeRole hops from a low-privilege starting identity, driven entirely by missing trust-policy conditions rather than an application vulnerability.

summary.root_cause: Both trust policies in the chain permitted sts:AssumeRole from a broad Principal (account root / prior role ARN) with no sts:ExternalId, aws:SourceIp, aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent, or sts:DurationSeconds condition.
